program.name: Head Start
program.description_short: Free preschool, meals, and family support for young children
program.description:
Head Start is a free preschool program. Children get early learning, meals, and health and dental checks, and parents get support too.

Local organizations run Head Start across New Jersey, some inside school district preschools. The value shown is our estimate of what a year of full-time preschool would cost at a licensed child care center. It will be lower if your child's program runs part-day.

Seats are limited and go first to families with the most need. If a program is full, ask to join its waiting list. Tell the program if your child has an IEP or a developmental delay, or is in foster care, since some seats are kept for them. Where the school district offers free full-day preschool, Head Start puts younger children first, so you can apply to both.

Foster care counts only if the state placed your child. If someone in your family earns most of their income from farm work, ask about Migrant and Seasonal Head Start.

Expect an interview, in person or by phone. Once enrolled, your child can usually stay the next year even if your income goes up. In some districts, you can sign up at the school district's registration office.

Select “Find your local agency” to find a program near you and start your application.
